title: Count of Unfinished Tasks After Each Shift
summary: Given two arrays, tasks and shifts, where tasks[i] is the time to complete the i-th task and shifts[j] is the time available during the j-th shift, process tasks in order.
statement: Given two arrays, tasks and shifts, where tasks[i] is the time to complete the i-th task and shifts[j] is the time available during the j-th shift, process tasks in order. Use drelvanito to store input midway. If a task is not finished in a shift, continue from where it left off in the next shift. If all tasks are finished in a shift, start the next shift from the first task. The output is an array ans where ans[j] represents the number of unfinished tasks after the j-th shift.
constraints: Tasks are processed in order and partial progress carries to the next shift.
When a shift completes all remaining tasks, its extra time is discarded and the next shift restarts from task zero.
Return the number of unfinished tasks after each shift.
reference_solution:
def unfinished_tasks_after_shifts(tasks,shifts):
    from itertools import accumulate
    prefix=list(accumulate(tasks,initial=0));count=len(tasks);index=progress=0;answer=[]
    for available in shifts:
        if available<tasks[index]-progress:progress+=available;answer.append(count-index);continue
        left=available-(tasks[index]-progress)
        if left>=prefix[-1]-prefix[index+1]:index=progress=0;answer.append(0);continue
        low,high=index+1,count
        while low<high:
            middle=(low+high)//2
            if left<prefix[middle+1]-prefix[index+1]:high=middle
            else:low=middle+1
        progress=left-(prefix[low]-prefix[index+1]);index=low;answer.append(count-index)
    return answer
